nodes.body: This guard now diagnoses the existing SM120 round-trip fixture's `IMAD.WIDE.U32 R2, R7, 0x4, R2` and `... R4` instructions because their scalar multiplier is an immediate rather than `UR`. That fixture still asserts empty diagnostics and the generated `mul.wide.u32`/`add.u64` at `ptx/tests/sass_lifter_fuzz.rs:151-164`, so the current test suite fails. Either retain a compatible narrow path for these existing immediate forms or update the fixture and support contract together.

This new declaration path also covers the existing `ATOMG.E.ADD.STRONG.GPU ... desc[UR6][R8.64]` fixture, but only `load_op` and `store_op` call `desc_address_pair_setup`; `atomic_op` formats `[%rd8]` directly. The resulting PTX uses an uninitialized `%rd8` instead of the `{%r8, %r9}` address pair. Add the predicated descriptor setup in `atomic_op` using its computed address index, or diagnose descriptor-address atomics as unsupported.

Numeric width modifiers are kept in `inst.modifiers` while `data_type` remains unset (`disassembler.rs:539-548` and `SassDataType::from_modifier` does not map `64`/`128`). Consequently `LDG.E.64`/`STG.E.64` (and `.128`) bypass this predicate and fall through to `load_op`/`store_op`, which emit `.u32` instead of rejecting the unsupported wide access. Detect the numeric width modifiers and all data types wider than 32 bits here.

The new `IADD.64` lowering path has no unit fixture, while the surrounding lifter has extensive instruction-level tests. Add a predicated case covering an `R` first source, an `UR` second source, pair unpacking, and the unsupported-form diagnostic so the new register-pair bridge is protected.
